text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about these frightening episodes, such as whether you can be easily comforted or if you remember the dreams the next morning? Also, do you snore loudly or gasp for air while you sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any specific scary dreams during these episodes, or do you wake up abruptly without remembering any dream content? Also, have you noticed any recent changes in your stress levels, school performance, or home environment that might be causing anxiety?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you recall the bad dreams, this points more toward nightmares than night terrors. Do you have any fears about going to bed or going to school, and does your sleep improve if you stay up later?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she exhibit any other symptoms of anxiety, such as excessive worrying, restlessness, or difficulty concentrating during the day? I would also like to rule out any underlying sleep disorders like sleep apnea, so I will request a sleep study. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
